text: North Red Deer was a former village in central Alberta, Canada, located within the City of Red Deer. It was situated on the north shore of the Red Deer River along the Calgary and Edmonton (C&E) Railway, which was later acquired by the Canadian Pacific Railway. The former village is now part of Red Deer's Riverside Meadows neighbourhood, with some areas also falling within Highland Green and Oriole Park. Established as a hamlet in 1894 following the completion of the C&E rail line and the construction of the bridge over the Red Deer River, North Red Deer incorporated as the Village of North Red Deer on February 17, 1911, with the ministerial order signed on June 18, 1911. Walter Webb served as the village's first mayor, beginning on March 13, 1911. After an earlier unratified effort in 1946, the village officially amalgamated with the City of Red Deer on January 1, 1948, with the last village council meeting held on December 24, 1947. In 1999, the City of Red Deer renamed the area to Riverside Meadows. In 2000, the city adopted the Riverside Meadows Area Redevelopment Plan (ARP), which was later replaced by a new ARP in 2009. The city marked the centennial of the Village of North Red Deer on August 27, 2011. During its existence, the population grew from 304 in 1911 to 698 in 1946.
